subject: HealthCore: follow-up on Private upgrade - control plane regressions and next steps
messages:
From: Elaine Cho <ops@healthcore.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-leads@healthcore.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 08:47:12 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Post-upgrade issues: control plane timeouts

Marissa / Redwood team,

We completed the scheduled Private control plane upgrade (v2.14.1) in our staging cluster at 03:15 PT and rolled the change to prod at 04:10. Starting ~04:40 we began seeing sustained partial connectivity failures between our VPC agents and the control plane — API requests to the management endpoint returned 504 or timed out after several seconds. This caused intermittent inference restarts and a spike in 5xx on a small subset of customer-facing routes.

Attached is a pcap capture and a short excerpt from our side showing repeated TLS handshake retries to the control plane IPs and several RSTs. We've opened a ticket (HC-5312) but wanted to escalate directly since this started right after the Redwood upgrade window.

Symptoms:
- Increased 502/504s from the agent->management calls starting ~04:40
- KV cache misses and occasional cold-start latency on a few nodes
- No obvious CPU or memory spike on our side; network shows repeated SYN/RST cycles to the control plane VIP

Can your team confirm whether there were any kernel-level changes, TLS rotation, or LB config changes tied to the deployment? We're paused on rolling the rest of our fleet until we get a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Elaine Cho
Platform Ops | HealthCore Labs

Attachment(s): healthcore-tcpdump-0609.pcap

Elaine — thanks for flagging this and for the pcap. Really sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev-2 while we triage; I've looped in Rishi (serving runtime) and Aditya (CS) to coordinate.

Immediate plan (next 90 minutes):
- Rishi to run an initial correlation of control plane logs vs. the HealthCore pcap and confirm whether our LB rotated certs / altered SNI on the upgrade.
- Aditya to schedule a 30-min bridge with your team for 09:45 PT and gather any additional traces.
- If we confirm a regression on our side we'll prepare a targeted rollback for the affected control plane pool.

Could you please:
1) Share the output of `curl -v` to the management endpoint from one of the affected nodes (pastebin or attach).
2) If possible, hold off on further fleet rollouts until we determine root cause.

We will follow up on this thread with a technical update and any mitigation we apply.

Apologies again — we'll get a fix or a documented rollback plan shortly.

—Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 12:03:44 -0700
Subject: RE: [URGENT] Post-upgrade issues: control plane timeouts

Marissa / Elaine — preliminary findings from our side after correlating HealthCore's pcap with our control plane telemetry:

Summary (TL;DR):
- The v2.14.1 rollout included an upstream LB change that added a connection keepalive tweak and a new TLS stack optimization. Under a specific client-side retransmit pattern (present in HealthCore's agent), the LB intermittently sent RSTs to rebalanced connections. This manifested as TLS handshake restarts and 504s for a subset of long-lived agent connections.

Root cause:
1) LB keepalive behavior + aggressive connection rebalancing after node rotation.
2) A subtle regression in our TLS session resumption path that failed to advertise expected session tickets when the agent reconnected quickly.

Impact:
- Affects Private control plane pools that used the rolling LB config (pilot ~20% of customers during this upgrade).
- For HealthCore it produced repeated short-lived disconnects and KV cache thrash on ~8 nodes for ~35 minutes.

Actions taken:
- We immediately reverted the LB keepalive tweak at 11:40 PT and re-applied the previous loopback policy; this reduced RSTs and stabilized handshakes within ~6 minutes.
- We pushed a hotfix to the TLS resumption code (candidate v2.14.2-hotfix) and staged it to a canary pool.
- We've prepared a rollback playbook if HealthCore prefers us to revert your control plane pool to the pre-upgrade state.

Attached: excerpt from control plane logs showing the RST cohort and our runbook patch.

Next steps:
- Marissa / Aditya: recommend offering HealthCore the choice of immediate rollback of their pool to pre-2.14.1 or applying the hotfix and monitoring for 1 hour.
- Rishi: will follow up with a short postmortem doc and the mitigations we committed to (LB policy guardrails + TLS resumption tests).

Elaine — apologies again. We're available for the 09:45 bridge if you still want to run through traces together (Aditya will coordinate the invite).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: HealthCore: post-incident update and customer-facing summary (June 9)

Elaine — thanks again for working through this with us. Below is a concise customer-facing summary you can share with your platform team and execs.

What happened (plain language):
- During our June 9 Private control plane upgrade we rolled a change to the load balancer keepalive behavior and a TLS session resumption optimization. Under a specific reconnect pattern present in HealthCore's agents, the LB occasionally reset connections while the agent retried, which led to transient management API timeouts and a small number of 5xx errors.

What we did:
- Immediately reverted the LB keepalive tweak (~11:40 PT) which significantly reduced connection resets.
- Deployed a hotfix to the TLS resumption path and validated it on a canary pool.
- Prepared a rollback playbook and are ready to revert HealthCore's pool to the pre-upgrade image if you prefer that route.

Impact to HealthCore:
- ~35 minutes of elevated 502/504s on a small subset of nodes; no data loss; inference workloads recovered once connections stabilized.

Compensation and next steps: 
- As this was caused by our upgrade regression, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equivalent to 2 hours of Dedicated control plane uptime for the affected cluster. Aditya will follow up on the exact billing adjustment and a support ticket update (HC-5312).
- Rishi's team will run an additional TLS session-resumption regression test suite against HealthCore's agent binary before the next scheduled upgrade.
- We'll schedule a short postmortem call next week to review the runbook and any adjustments you want us to make to your rollout cadence.

If you'd prefer we revert your cluster to the pre-upgrade image instead of applying the hotfix, reply 'ROLLBACK' and we'll initiate the rollback within the next maintenance window.

Again — sincerely sorry for the incident. We're tightening preflight checks and LB guardrails to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
